title: Second Issue of the Auxiliary Power Unit Aft Mount Standard with Spherical Bearing and Access Cut-Out
abstract: Second issue of the aft mount standard, replacing the plain bushes with a spherical bearing that accepts the misalignment the first issue could not, and cutting an inspection window in the heat shield.

sections.reason: The steel link and replaceable bush of the first issue removed the link replacement cost but did not remove the wear itself, and operators with the highest auxiliary power unit utilisation were still finding bushes at the limit at each heat check. Measurement of the installed geometry on twelve aircraft found a consistent angular misalignment at the aft attachment, produced by thermal growth of the tail cone structure relative to the unit. A plain bush cannot accept angular movement and simply wears until it can. The second driver came from the operators directly: the inspection cannot be done without dropping the aft heat shield, which adds six hours to a two hour task.
sections.description: The plain bushes introduced by the first issue are replaced by a self-aligning spherical bearing at the aft end of the link, which accepts the measured angular misalignment without edge loading. The link D4910124356332 is retained with a re-machined outer end, the bracket D4910125048089 is retained unchanged, and the seal D4910125265005 is added at the bearing to keep the tail cone environment out. The clamp assembly D4910128597967 is added to restrain the drain line that the larger bearing housing displaces. An inspection window is cut in the aft heat shield and closed with a removable panel, so that the bearing can be inspected without dropping the shield. Wiring at FIN 2PB7 is unchanged and the tube support at FIN 5401PA1 is repositioned 30 mm outboard. Work is in zones 313, 325 and 322 and is detailed on drawings D49101239814 and D49101253742.
sections.effects: Additional mass increase of 2.2 kg per aircraft above the first issue, aft of the reference station, with a centre-of-gravity effect that remains within the amendment already made. No electrical effect. The spherical bearing standard requires the first issue as a prerequisite because it re-machines the steel link introduced there; it cannot be applied to an aluminium link. Dispatch is unchanged. The mount inspection interval doubles and its elapsed time falls from eight hours to two because the heat shield stays in place. Maintenance, illustrated parts and the crew procedure for auxiliary power unit shutdown limits all require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN T00205 in February 2023. Retrofit through the modification bulletin, about one shift on aircraft already at the first issue standard. A second bulletin issued at the same time covers the heat shield window alone, for operators who want the inspection access before they take the bearing.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of reference station, within the existing weight and balance amendment
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00205, no line stoppage
